R6V-bear-backcountry-0002.name: 2.7 km NW of Blue River
R6V-bear-backcountry-0002.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).

evidence.t: Burn from 2022 (fire R90436), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SE facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 80 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Northern Rockies Regional Municipality, about 430 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 59.44958, -129.21843, pull off on Hwy 37 (paved road). Map links below.
Walk: 38 km N, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 1,086 m, about 861 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 140 m NE of the spot at 986 m (59.77513, -129.40351). Water: unnamed wetland 130 m S (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-24, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2025-06-05, closures 2026-10-16.
R6V-bear-backcountry-0002.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 6-24: about 108 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.01 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
